title: Make drain work user-queued (ask --later) requests too
summary: steward::queued_work keeps only channel "steward", so requests from `ask --later` (channel "cli") are never drained. Include both channels in the shared selection, keep ordering and retry rules unchanged, and prove it with tests using fresh ids. Audience: the user who queues requests and expects drain to work them.

defaults_applied.how: Fix the shared channel filter, not the named jobs.
New tests plus cargo test, clippy, fmt pass.
Criteria run tests with fresh ids showing drain works the cli request.
Docs and decision entry explain the change for outside readers.
One focused change to queue selection with docs.
Verifier runs the named cargo test commands.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: `ask --later` records channel "cli" (as the earlier reading found); the fix is the channel filter in queued_work at steward.rs ~line 341.
Selection is by channel set, never by job id; tests use ids other than the four named ones.
Final report should include a criterion-to-evidence table, but that is a report-format matter, not a repository deliverable.
Retry and ordering logic (received_at, then job id) stay untouched.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in steward.rs, with job ids unlike the named ones, shows queued_work returns unread Queued requests from both the steward and cli channels, oldest first (ties by job id), and excludes non-Queued jobs and other channels. Run `cargo test -p athena-core queued_work`.
A drain test with a cli-channel queued request (fresh id) in the records shows drain's queue lists it and works it in the same way as a steward item. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.
Existing drain ordering and retry/thrash tests pass unchanged and are not edited to fit. Run `cargo test`.
The change is a channel-set filter in queued_work (steward.rs), with no job-id special case; a grep of the diff finds none of the named ids in non-test code.

Doc comments saying drain takes only the steward channel (steward.rs REQUEST_CHANNEL, drain.rs, docs/decisions.md ~line 2206 area) are corrected, and a new decision entry and a CHANGELOG line record the change and why.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.

out_of_scope: Changing drain ordering, retry or thrash rules
Adding a harness gate for producer reports (already tried in earlier cases)
departures: Slightly lower acceptance than reference because the prior attempt failed on the structural criterion; the retry criteria are made concrete.
